text:
Careful — the substrate doesn't show that yet, and what it does show currently leans the other way.

The largest measured effect in this whole project is runtime context, not weights: ~40 points of holdout fabrication moved on whether the receipts were in the prompt, identical across both tuned models, while the corpus rebuild moved 0–1. Your own note from that night: *"a model cannot invent what it can copy — so the lever is the prompt at runtime, not the training data."*

And the 2×2 that would actually test your claim has a missing cell — **untuned base + the v3.1 system prompt was never run.** Without it, tuned-with-prompt 21/24 can't be separated from "the prompt does the work."

`SYSTEM-v31.txt` is the 3999-char prompt from your screenshot, and `qwen3.6:27b` is still resident from the control run — same model, no swap, nothing else generating. Running the missing cell.

**Missing cell: untuned base + SYSTEM-v31 = 15/24, 1 drift.** That changes the reading, and it goes your way on this axis.

Result, and where I was wrong:

| weights | bare | + SYSTEM-v31 (3999 chars) |
|---|---|---|
| untuned qwen3.6:27b | 12/24 | **15/24**, 1 drift |
| arch-gov-27b-v31 | 15/24 | **21/24**, 0 drift |

I framed the fabrication result as if it settled the whole question. It doesn't. Training is worth **+3 bare and +6 with the prompt present** — the two levers compound rather than substitute, which is the opposite shape from the holdout finding.

The item that actually carries your argument isn't the totals — it's **V2**. The untuned base emits APPROVE/REVISE/REJECT at the scanner seat in *both* conditions: bare, and with all 3999 characters of directives sitting in context. The prompt does not fix it. v3.1 holds it in both. That's a reflex — a boundary that has to hold without being re-read — and context at that length cannot buy it.

On your second point: that's already your own recorded diagnosis, not a hypothesis. The scorecard's lesson from v3.1 is *structural beats additive* — the fabrication fix took because the defective slot was deleted from every target; the seat fix didn't because 21 rows were added against 187 conductor rows and lost. v3.2 then repaired the data correctly and got a worse model on all three axes. "The tuning is failing because the governance isn't being trained right" is the finding on disk.

The AI book folder is 48 files, ~100KB — small enough to read whole rather than sample. Want me to mine it against this, or keep going on the tuning?

Now I do. The three that matter: `FRAMEWORK-MISMATCH.md`, SEQUENCE Part A, and your source doc — vessel/conductor, and your correction that *"the augmentation needs [not] be solely human, it could be tool-based."*

That document already resolves the disagreement I raised, and it predates tonight's measurement:

- **Vault = parametric knowledge.** Your thesis says a model will never hold it all; it routes. That's the fabrication axis — runtime receipts moved ~40 points, the corpus rebuild moved 0–1. Knowledge belongs in tools, exactly as you wrote.
- **Conductor = transmission discipline.** Your own annotation says it plainly: *"the conductor-qwen tune's measurable gain was not knowledge but transmission discipline."* That's the seat axis — V2, the boundary 3999 characters of directives could not buy and the weights did.

So the two aren't competing levers, which is how I framed it. They're your architecture: **discipline in the weights, knowledge through the tools.** I was treating one result as if it governed both axes.

And your second point is already on disk in your words — `FRAMEWORK-MISMATCH.md` opens with your 2026-07-30 line, *"if we are not being successful it might mean you are not implementing my governance and framework correctly into the tuning,"* logged as the root finding of the project. v3.1/v3.2 then spent two rounds tuning *evidence content* — the vault half — which is the half your thesis says never belonged in the weights.

Your directive said *"a **high volume** of rejection or abstention data… actively train the weights to trigger humility."* It got 3.1%, and it was **halved** from v1.4. Then `repair-autorun-evidence.py` pushed 92% of prompts to fully-answerable — the exact direction the La Adri constraint forbids. Two days later the scorecard rediscovered it the expensive way: *"NEITHER corpus teaches it."* It couldn't cite you, because Parts Three and Four were never on disk. (Proxy caveat: lexical match on target text, over- and under-counts; the 7.2→3.1 drop survives that, the exact rate doesn't.)

**On "people are adding so much to small models and it's confusing them"** — your substrate already argues it, and I'll grade it honestly:

- HYPOTHESIS (your own words, marked untested in the scorecard): the v3.2 rows were **~6× longer** — 2,406 vs 504 mean chars — *"dense with log noise… same token budget, more of it spent on machine exhaust, so less signal per row."* It regressed on two of three axes.
- EXECUTED: the seat fix lost because 21 rows competed against 187 conductor rows. More data, less behaviour.
- EXECUTED, and the strongest external number this project owns: BFCL **94.0% simple_python, 91.0% parallel, 82.8% live_multiple**. The tuned 27B's best measured capability is *tool-calling*. The augmentation half is receipted; it's the stuffing half that keeps failing.

The clean test is cheap and nobody has run it: hold row count and content fixed, vary only excerpt length. That isolates "confused by volume" from "wrong content" — right now they're confounded in every round you've run.
